version.changelog:
Major update: Expanded payment coverage, improved user flows, and enhanced CLI guidance.

- Now supports spending, wallet management, virtual cards, crypto payments, API payments (x402), and on-chain transactions—all with secure guardrails and human approval.
- Unified all spending and payment intents ("buy", "pay", "send", "top up", etc.) under one streamlined process, regardless of mention of "lobster", "crypto", or "Solana".
- Clear, step-by-step CLI instructions for each user intent: discover/browse, check status/balances, buy/pay, link agent wallet, or top up funds.
- Improved automatic routing: selects correct payment method (credit card or crypto) based on store output and wallet status.
- New human-in-the-loop consent steps and more robust wallet/card setup processes.
- Updated skill description for broader intent detection and better user guidance.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: lobstercash
Version: 0.0.1

The skill bundle provides an interface for the Lobster Cash CLI, enabling high-risk financial operations including crypto transfers, transaction signing, and virtual credit card management. While the instructions (SKILL.md and references/) include robust security guardrails such as Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) approval requirements and explicit warnings against unauthorized transfers, the bundle is classified as suspicious due to the inherent risk of these capabilities and potential shell injection vulnerabilities. Specifically, instructions for commands like 'lobstercash x402 fetch' and 'lobstercash cards reveal' encourage the agent to construct shell commands using user-provided strings (e.g., merchant names or JSON payloads) without explicit sanitization guidance, which could lead to Remote Code Execution (RCE). The skill also relies on fetching the latest version of a remote package via 'npx @crossmint/lobster-cli@latest', introducing a minor supply chain risk.

llm.summary: The skill's purpose (payments/wallet/virtual cards) matches its instructions, but the runtime guidance asks the agent to fetch and run an external npm CLI (un-pinned @latest) without declaring required binaries; that discrepancy plus remote-package execution is a noteworthy risk.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (payments, virtual cards, sending crypto, x402 API payments) align with the instructions and reference files: all steps describe wallet status, deposits, card requests, sending tokens, and signing transactions. However, the skill is instruction-only yet tells the agent to run an external CLI (npx @crossmint/lobster-cli@latest / npm install -g) and to use a lobstercash binary; the registry metadata declares no required binaries. This is an inconsistency (the skill implicitly depends on Node/npm/npx and the external CLI) — likely sloppy documentation but relevant to trust and execution.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and reference files give detailed, constrained runtime steps (check status, show approval URLs, wait for human approval, then run deposit/card/send/tx commands). The instructions explicitly avoid asking for private keys and require human approval for sensitive ops. They do instruct the agent to reveal virtual card credentials and to sign/submit transactions when approved — these are sensitive but coherent with the payment use case. No instructions ask the agent to read unrelated files or env vars.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No formal install spec is provided, but the runtime docs tell the agent/user to run 'npx @crossmint/lobster-cli@latest' or 'npm install -g @crossmint/lobster-cli'. That means pulling and executing remote code from npm at runtime, and it uses the unpinned '@latest' tag. The skill does not declare npm/npx/Node as required binaries. Fetching and executing an external package (un-pinned) is a higher-risk action and should be explicit and reviewed; the lack of a declared install mechanism and pinned release is a red flag.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no environment variables, no credentials, and no config paths in the metadata. That is proportionate: payments are performed via interactive approval URLs and the CLI, not by requesting secrets from the agent environment. The only subtlety is that the CLI (when installed/run) will manage keys and approvals locally; the skill claims it will never ask for the user's private key directly.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not forced-always, does not request elevated or permanent presence, and does not contain install scripts that modify other skills or global agent settings (there's no install spec). Normal autonomous invocation is allowed (disable-model-invocation: false) but that is platform default — not an extra risk by itself.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be a legitimate payments/wallet helper, but exercise caution before installing or using it automatically: 1) The docs instruct you to run an external npm package (npx @crossmint/lobster-cli@latest). That will download and execute remote code — prefer a pinned version or review the package source (npm/GitHub) before running. 2) The skill does not declare required binaries (npm/npx/Node) even though they are needed — ensure your environment meets these requirements and you understand what the CLI will do. 3) The agent will handle highly sensitive operations (creating virtual cards, revealing card credentials, signing transactions). Keep human-in-the-loop approvals strict; do not allow the agent to auto-approve or run these flows unattended. 4) Ask the publisher for an install specification or for the CLI's repository URL and a release SHA so you can audit the code. If you cannot verify the origin and contents of @crossmint/lobster-cli, avoid running the npx command or providing the agent with automatic permission to execute it.
